'''''Cistanche phelypaea''''', also spelled '''''Cistanche phelipaea''''', is a species of plant in the family [[Orobanchaceae]]. It has a wide range of distribution from the [[Arabian Peninsula]] and the [[Syrian Desert]] in the east, through the [[Sahara]], [[Cyprus]], [[Crete]] and the southwest of the [[Iberian Peninsula]], to [[Macaronesia]] in the west.

==Description==
[[File:Cistanche phelypaea Sal Cape Verde 01.jpg|thumb|left|''Cistanche phelypaea'']]
''Cistanche phelypaea'' is a chlorophyll-free, obligate parasitic plant with stout fleshy flowering stems bearing bright yellow flowers and rising to {{convert|20|-|50|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall from a generally swollen base.<ref name="kenfern">{{cite web |title=Cistanche phelypaea |url=http://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Cistanche%20phelypaea |publisher=Tropical Plants Database, Ken Fern |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="iberica" /> The stem is [[Glabrousness (botany)|glabrous]] and yellow to purple gray. Leaves are ovate-lanceolate, obtuse, glabrous and normally brown in color. [[Inflorescence]] is dense, more or less cylindrical. Flower crown is broadly campanulate-obconic, strongly curved, bright yellow, sometimes light purple, and glabrous. It has white stigmatic lobes. 2n = 40; n = 20.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Cistanche phelypaea |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/14_05%20cistanche.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref> It parasites roots of [[Chenopodiaceae]] bushes.<ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Cistanche phelypaea (L.) Cout. |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1cistanche+phelypaea |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref> The plant is used a food source and is eaten similar to [[asparagus]].<ref name="kenfern" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Cistanche phelypaea'' inhabits saline, sandy, mainly coastal zones but also inland sites from sea level up to {{convert|600|m|ft|abbr=on}} altitude. In West Asia it occupies [[Syria]], [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Qatar]], [[Oman]], [[Yemen]], [[Soqotra]]; in Africa, [[Djibouti]], [[Ethiopia]], [[Eritrea]], [[Sudan]], [[Egypt]], [[Chad]], [[Libya]], [[Niger]], [[Algeria]], [[Tunisia]], [[Mali]], [[Senegal]], [[Mauritania]], [[Western Sahara]], [[Morocco]]; in Southern Europe, [[Cyprus]], [[Crete]], [[Spain]], [[Portugal]]; in [[Macaronesia]], [[Cape Verde]], [[Canary Islands]], [[Savage Islands]] and [[Madeira]].<ref name="iberica" /><ref name="CoL">{{cite web |title=Cistanche phelipaea (L.) Cout. |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/VL7Y |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref> It has also been introduced in [[Mozambique]] and [[France]].<ref name="CoL" />
